title: Car Fleet
prompt:
There are `n` cars traveling to the same destination along a one-lane road. The destination is `target` miles away. You're given arrays `position` and `speed`, where `position[i]` is the starting position of the `i`-th car (all positions are unique) and `speed[i]` is its speed. A car can never pass another car ahead of it, but it can catch up and drive at the same speed, forming a car fleet that travels together at the slower car's speed.

A car fleet is a set of cars that arrive at the destination at the same time. Return the number of distinct car fleets that will arrive at the destination.

examples.explanation: Cars starting at 10 and 8 form one fleet (8 catches up to 10). The car at 0 travels alone. Cars at 5 and 3 form another fleet.
Every car eventually merges into a single fleet by the time they reach the target.

constraints: All values of position are unique
hints: Only relative order and time-to-reach-target matter — a car merges into the fleet ahead of it if it would otherwise catch up before or exactly at the target.
Sort cars by starting position (closest to target first) and compute each car's time to reach target if it never had to slow down: (target - position) / speed.

Process cars from closest to target to farthest, maintaining a stack of 'fleet arrival times'. A car joins the fleet ahead (doesn't form a new one) if its own solo time is <= the time on top of the stack; otherwise it forms a new fleet and its time is pushed.

solution.approach: Sort cars by starting position in descending order (closest to the target first), since a car can only ever be blocked by cars ahead of it. For each car compute its unobstructed time to reach the target: (target - position) / speed. Walk through cars from closest to farthest, maintaining a stack of fleet arrival times. If the current car's own time is <= the time on top of the stack, it will catch up to and merge into that fleet (never overtaking), so it doesn't start a new fleet. Otherwise it arrives strictly later than the fleet ahead, so it's slower and forms its own new fleet — push its time. The final stack size is the number of fleets.
